newsitem.title: USA: TCI preliminary report shows higher revenues.
newsitem.headline: TCI preliminary report shows higher revenues.

text.p: TCI Communications Inc. Thursday said it expects third quarter revenues and cash flow to be higher than a year ago but rising expense levels have forced the company to ask its major equipment suppliers to suspend shipments immediately.

In a statement, TCI Communications, the core cable operations of Tele-Communications Inc., said preliminary estimates showed third quarter revenues rose to $1.65 billion, up from $1.31 billion in the year-earlier period and cash flow rose to $591 million from $526 million last year.

Industry analysts have been concerned about the company's cash flow, which is roughly pre-tax profits plus other items, after TCI told 30 major vendors to halt shipments of equipment until further notice in order to ensure successful deployment of inventory and control unnecessary capital spending.
News of the request was first reported Wednesday by cable television station CNBC.
In its statement, TCI said revenues were strong during the quarter but expenses were also higher.

"Overall, the third quarter shows strong revenue growth in TCIC's core cable operations and major progress on its new product introductions," said Brendan Clouston, chief executive of TCI Communications, the cable unit.
"Due primarily to new product start-up costs and the timing of cost efficiencies the company expects to realise in the near future, third quarter expense levels are temporarily elevated," he added.
TCI has been on an ambitious quest to introduce new products such as telephone service and digital television.

The preliminary revenue and cash flow figures include two months' results of cable systems acquired from Viacom Inc, as well as Primestar by TCI, a direct broadcast service and telephony and digital TV business units.

TCI said its consolidated customer base stood at 13.947 million customers, compared with 12.987 at the end of the second quarter. But the increase was due to acquisitions with TCI losing some customers during the summer due to a recent rate hike and the summer lull in the entertainment business.
TCI's stock, which has been under pressure recently, lost 50 cents to close at $11.625, just above its 52-week low of $11.3125.
The spokeswoman said that, following the usual summer lull, the company did see some increase in customer numbers in the first week of September.
